newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares slide at close on foreign selling.
newsitem.headline: KL shares slide at close on foreign selling.

text.p: Malaysian shares slid to another sharp fall at the close on Tuesday as foreign institutional funds sold down in an already nervous market, analysts and dealers said.

At the close of trade, the benchmark Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks dropped 14.42 points, or 1.31 percent, to 1,086.67. It had fallen to as low as 1,080.83, a new intraday low for the year.
"I have been selling for foreign clients today, and I have even been shorting," said a dealer at a bank-backed brokerage.

Sentiment had been battered on fears over earnings growth potentials of several banks with exposures to property lending and share financing, after the central bank imposed measures to curtail speculation within the sectors.
The measures had caused clients with leveraged positions to either top up their portfolios with cash, or sell down their holdings.

Rumours that several stockbroking houses had been suspended from trading for exceeding their lending limits appeared unfounded as fund managers and dealers said they had executed trades through the firms.
